points.description: States that a class can have an unlimited (any) number of constructors — accept 'unlimited', 'infinite', 'as many as you want', 'no limit', 'any number', or equivalent wording. A specific finite number (e.g. 'two', 'three') or a bare 'more than one' does not earn full marks.
points.partial_credit: Partial marks for answers that show several constructors are allowed but do not say the number is unlimited.

levels.says: Says a class can have more than one / several / multiple constructors, without stating that the number is unlimited.
Says only that a class has at least one constructor, or gives a small finite number of constructors (e.g. two or three) as the answer.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the idea that the number of constructors for a class is unlimited (any number, no limit). Answers saying only that several or more than one constructor is possible earn half marks, and answers giving just one or a small fixed number earn a small part. A blank or irrelevant answer earns nothing.
